Purpuric retiform patches on each flank
CT chest/abdomen: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia
Punch biopsy findings: Small organisms within vasculature
Tissue Gram staining: Gram-positive cocci in vessels
diffuse papules on the trunk and extremities
Purpuric retiform patches on each flank
CT chest/abdomen: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia
Punch biopsy findings: Small organisms within vasculature
Tissue Gram staining: Gram-positive cocci in vessels

concepts.why: The patient presented with fever, abdominal pain, and vomiting, and laboratory tests showed hyponatremia, neutropenia, and elevated C-reactive protein, indicating a severe infection.
The CT chest/abdomen showed cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia.
The CT chest/abdomen showed areas of nonenhancement within both kidneys suspected to represent renal abscesses.
The MRI brain showed multifocal lesions, likely septic emboli, and the punch biopsy findings showed small organisms within vasculature.
The patient presented with purpuric retiform patches on each flank and diffuse papules on the trunk and extremities, indicating a severe vasculitic process.

rationales.F06: Purpuric retiform patches are characteristic of Purpura fulminans and suggest Staphylococcal sepsis.
rationales.F10: Necrotizing pneumonia is a strong indicator of C02.
rationales.F11: Small organisms within vasculature suggest Staphylococcal sepsis.
rationales.F12: Gram-positive cocci in vessels are characteristic of Staphylococcal sepsis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of small organisms within vasculature, Gram-positive cocci in vessels, and positive tissue, blood, and fluid cultures support Staphylococcal sepsis, which explains the systemic findings including fever, elevated C-reactive protein, and multi-organ involvement.
